admission.justification: Without the collection a finished master with housekeeping left over is refused and the operator is sent to run `worktree_cleanup` by hand before a reopen that can do it through the same transaction; without the line rule a leaf that legitimately landed twice forces a hand-edit of a contract cell, which is the repair the product itself created. The two tests pin both paths end to end.

applicability: Reopening a completed atomic master, and the closeout chain proof that follows a leaf which landed, was reopened and landed again.
conditions: The leaf's master and its branches exist, or the master's sprint records status inProgress.
The current leaf contract equals the reopened contract of an archive whose cleanup completed, and the archive and its receipt stay readable.
No code or memory worktree of the reopened contract exists: a started generation is live work, not a reset waiting to happen.
The review and memory-review round counts restart for the new delivery while earlier rounds and verdicts stay in the record.
The reopen-reset state is accepted only while the surviving contract is exactly the reopen's reset of the archived contract; any other contract still meets the archive refusal.
A missing master or a closed sprint is answered by naming it, not by a new refusal, and the landing-ancestry checks and fast-forward-only integration stay as they are.

A completed master with `cleanup: pending` reopens only when its closeout and its integration both record `completed`; the collection runs through the product's own cleanup transaction, the plan is built from the contract that collection left behind, and a dry run collects nothing.

The chain origin is the master's line, not one exact commit: the oldest landed leaf's base and the master's recorded base have to lie on one line in either direction, and an off-line position refuses `atomic-series-leaf-chain-invalid` naming `worktree_integrate` on the leaf or `worktree_sync` on the master, never an edit of a contract cell.
exclusions: Writing, moving or deleting archive bytes, receipts or landed commits: the reopen collects through the existing transaction.

evidence: The four reopen arms, the third terminal-archive state, the reopened status projection and the start's prepared-start branch all exist at the reviewed freeze; the seven cases of mcp/tests/test_task_reopen_cycle.py drive them through the public entry points.

Ruling 7dc3b6d2 defect (b): `cleanup: pending` on a completed closeout is housekeeping left undone, so `_collect_completed_uncleaned` runs `cleanup_result` (the transaction `worktree_cleanup` runs) and `_admitted_series_reopen` plans from the reloaded contract; a mid-flight master keeps its refusal. Defect (a): `_require_chain_origin` now proves the oldest landed leaf's position on the master's line through `_require_chain_origin_on_line`, refusing only an off-line base with the integrate/sync remedy. `_commanding_sprint_state` supplies the sprint status that distinguishes a moved line from an inactive sprint.

statement: A completed task reopens from its master's state and completes again without limit: a leaf whose master and branches exist reopens from the master's current tip and a master reopens while its sprint is active, restored from the sprint's integration branch; a task already carrying the reopen tombstone answers `reopened` again with the same next step and writes nothing, while a live generation still meets the unchanged preflight refusal; the start after a reopen accepts the archived generation's reset contract, recreating the enclosure and naming `worktree_start` as the next step instead of refusing `terminal-archive-contract-mismatch`; a master's parent is its sprint, so `parent_task_name` is no longer an admission edge and the folder resolution uses the recorded value only when it names a folder other than the master's own; a master whose closeout and integration both completed but whose cleanup never ran reopens too, the reopen collecting the enclosure through the same cleanup transaction `worktree_cleanup` runs before it plans, while a master still in flight keeps its refusal; and the chain a master's closeout proves starts on the master's own line rather than at one exact commit, so a leaf that landed, was reopened and landed again is accepted at that later position in either direction, and only a position off the line refuses, naming `worktree_integrate` or `worktree_sync` rather than a contract-cell edit.
